result.summary: Allow `SignPSBTInput` to accept valid 65-byte Taproot signatures ending in `SIGHASH_ALL` when neither `PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE` nor an explicit sighash parameter is set. Previously, unset sighash types defaulted strictly to 64-byte `SIGHASH_DEFAULT` signatures, causing existing 65-byte `SIGHASH_ALL` signatures to fail validation.
result.problem: When processing Taproot inputs without an explicit sighash type, `SignPSBTInput` assumed `SIGHASH_DEFAULT` and rejected valid 65-byte `SIGHASH_ALL` signatures, preventing such PSBTs from being further signed or finalized.
evidence: Fixes #36507: 'PSBT: SignPSBTInput rejects valid 65-byte taproot script signatures when PSBT_IN_SIGHASH_TYPE is absent'
PR description: 'Its check of existing signatures then rejected every 65-byte taproot signature, so a PSBT holding a valid SIGHASH_ALL signature could be neither finalized nor signed further.'
result.scope_notes: Diff not provided in input; changes appear contained to PSBT signing logic and accompanying tests across two files.
result.card: Updates SignPSBTInput to accept 65-byte Taproot signatures ending in SIGHASH_ALL when sighash type is unspecified. Previously, unset sighash fields defaulted strictly to SIGHASH_DEFAULT, incorrectly rejecting 65-byte SIGHASH_ALL signatures and blocking finalization or further signing of affected PSBTs. This fixes issue #36507.

risk.why: Flaws in PSBT signature validation or sighash handling could cause invalid signatures to be accepted into PSBTs or break PSBT interoperability.
